## Chapter range

**Chapters 0171 to 0190 inclusive. Twenty chapters. Days 175 to 194 of the flood. One chapter to one day for days 175 to 193, and two chapters on day 194, which is 0190 and 0191 — and day 194 is one day and one weekday and the two chapters share both.**

Files are `chapters/volume-04/chapter-0171.md` through `chapter-0190.md`. The directory exists and has twenty files in it already; **do not restart, do not rewrite, and do not renumber Chapters 0151 to 0170.**

**This batch carries the volume's midpoint and the volume's only clock. Chapter 0175 is the day a household is asked for the days on its gate. Chapter 0185 is the day the quarter runs out. Nothing else in this batch is as important as those two chapters and nothing else may be treated as more important than they are.**

## Batch goal

**A family is asked for the days on its gate in a room, in daylight, with a date on it, and says yes, and it costs them their days and it costs Adrian his silence, and neither of them is a rescue. Then the quarter runs out on day 189 and nothing comes back from it, and a man who spent three volumes being the man who gives the only thing he has away is on the wrong side of a decision he dated himself, and the cost of the volume lands on a woman who has already said she is going to be angry about it for a year.**

## The beats, in order

1. **0171, day 175, Monday, the twentieth day of the Long Month.** The five days before the asking, with a date on it that eleven miles of Reach knows about and a gate that has a household behind it. **A boy of eight has been told and the telling is the chapter's work, and he is not a device and he is not a lesson and nobody improves on a child.**
2. **0172, day 176, Tuesday.** What the settlement does in the four days before it asks: it tells people, it reads a cost out again, it does not threaten anybody, **and it is at its most persuasive exactly when it is closest to succeeding.**
3. **0173, day 177, Wednesday.** The keeper's household, on its own ground, with the board and the rope and the boy, **and the chapter is the last one in this batch in which she is a person with a household rather than a decision somebody is waiting for.**
4. **0174, day 178, Thursday.** The day before. The weather turns. The rota on the gate board. **And Adrian is eleven miles away and has entered that he will not be asked to be, and he is not asked, and being right about that is not a comfort.**
5. **0175, day 179, Friday, the twenty-fourth day of the Long Month. THE VOLUME'S MIDPOINT.** **A household is asked, in a room, in daylight, with a date on it, for the whole of the days on the Redroot gate for the rest of the season.** It is not a purchase and it is not a seizure and the gate itself is not what is asked for. **The room is about nine people. The cost is read out first and it is true. The household says yes.** It is said by a person and not by a vote, because a count is a list. **The keeper does not say she would say yes again and does not say she is glad, and she has already said she is going to be angry about it for a year and nobody may improve on that. Adrian is not in the room and finds out afterwards and it is not from a page.**
6. **0176 to 0180, days 180 to 184.** The five days after. The wage is real, the racks are drying, the queue is a queue, the boy has a bed, and **the gate is still there and still belongs to the household and the only thing that is different is whose turn it is.** Nobody improves on this. **The finding of the week is that a gate is not owned and giving the days back means the gate never went anywhere.**
7. **0181 to 0184, days 185 to 188.** The pressure builds on the other side. The settlement is not a villain about it; **it is disappointed, and it says so, and its disappointment is the argument.** The player coalition splits. **Jonah Pike and Adrian are in a room and neither of them wins it and the thing that is settled is a date.**
8. **0185, day 189, Monday, the thirty-fourth day of the Long Month. THE QUARTER RUNS OUT.** **Thirty-five days after the hearing on day 154 and nothing can be put in front of that office and nothing can be prepared and no road reaches it.** What comes back is a number and the reading of that number is not Adrian's, **and it does not arrive on the day and that is the finding, because a thing that was going to arrive on a day and did not is a different kind of information from a thing that arrives.**
9. **0186 to 0190, days 190 to 194.** The cost, named out loud by the people paying it, and the beginning of the volume's last movement. **Chapter 0187, day 191, is a day the wall speaks: it repeats the number before it and the count of silences does not move on it.** **Chapter 0190, day 194, is the batch's cliff and it is the first of two chapters on that day.**

- **A weekday is a figure and day 1 is a Tuesday.** Every weekday above is computed from day 1 and from nothing else. **No chapter may take a weekday from a neighbouring chapter or from a day map.** The anchors a writer may check against: day 49 a Monday, day 100 a Wednesday, day 130 a Friday, day 131 a Saturday, day 154 a Monday, day 155 a Tuesday, day 156 a Wednesday, **day 174 a Sunday, day 179 a Friday, day 189 a Monday, day 194 a Saturday.**
- **Day 194 carries two chapters and one weekday.** In `outline/volume-04.md` §14.1 the double days are 194, 196, 198 and 200 and they are written `194 Sat +` and `194 Sun` and the weekday column gives both of them the same weekday. **They are both on day 194, a Saturday. There is no second day and no second weekday, and a chapter that says the second one happened on the Sunday has invented a day.**
- **The quarter runs out on day 189, a Monday**, thirty-five days after the hearing on day 154. **The days the quarter has left are 189 minus the day: fourteen at Chapter 0171, ten at the midpoint, one at Chapter 0184, and zero at Chapter 0185.**
- **The days the thirty-nine men under the near gate have gone unpaid are the day minus eighty-five**, because the first of March was the eighty-fifth day of this flood: ninety at Chapter 0171, ninety-four on the day of the asking, a hundred and four at Chapter 0185, a hundred and nine at Chapter 0190.
- **The count of silences is seventy-eight at Chapter 0170 and it stands there on day 174, because the wall spoke on day 173 and repeated the number before it and the count did not move.** The running figure is **one addition for each day the wall says nothing**, so days 174 to 190 are seventeen additions and the figure is **ninety-five at day 190**. **The wall speaks again on day 191, at Chapter 0187, and on that day it repeats the number before it and the count does not move, and the figure there is ninety-five.** **If the figure you compute and the figure printed in the last chapter written disagree, the rule is wrong and no figure is written until it is settled.** The figure is paid for at three points in this batch and not in every chapter.
- **No §23 figure changes and no §24 figure changes, because §23.19 is the close of Volume 03 and §24 is the close of the first twenty chapters of this volume.** Where this batch establishes something new it goes into a new section when the volume is written.
- **Date forms. Four, and only four.** *The Nth day of this flood* (1–40). *The Nth day of the new month* (26–90). *The Nth day of the month after this one* (91–155). ***The Nth day of the Long Month* (156–220, the Nth is day − 155).** **No chapter in this batch may use the first, second or third form for its own day.** The only two month names in this world are *March*, which is a day landmark and not a form, and *the Long Month*.

## The two chapters this batch exists for

### Chapter 0175 — day 179, Friday, the twenty-fourth day of the Long Month

**The household must be asked, in a room, in daylight, with a date on it, for the days on the Redroot gate.** The day is on the page already: it came back from the meeting-ground on a raft, the meeting-ground did not set it, and a woman with a board in her left hand chose it and said so at a door in Chapter 0170.

**What is asked for is a quantity of water on given weeks for the rest of the season. The gate is not being sold, cannot be sold, and nobody in the settlement's store is going to write the word *sold* on anything this month.** What is offered in return is a wage, a dry bed, a place at the front of a queue that works, a Warden, and a settlement that will hold the channel and clear the drain and stand four hundred and forty racks in any weather.

**Rules for the chapter, and they are the rules the volume turns on:**

- **The room is about nine people and it is a room and not a hall, and it is in daylight, and the date is on the door.**
- **The cost is read out before the asking, in full, in the words of the person offering it and not in the words of the person hearing it.**
- **The keeper's household says yes. It is said by a person. There is no count of hands, because a count is a list, and a list of who said what in a room is a removal with a column for where the person is.**
- **The keeper does not say she would say yes again. She does not say she is glad. She has already said she is going to be angry about it for a year and that is the whole of her, and nobody may improve on it, soften it, explain it or redeem it.**
- **She may not be rescued, may not be talked out of it, may not be given a reason to change her mind, and may not be a lesson.** She is a woman with a workway, a wage, nine days of racks saved, a child and a gate board.
- **Adrian is not in the room. He is not asked whether the day suits him. Nobody thinks of asking him because he is not a party to it. He finds out afterwards, and it is not from a page.**
- **The boy of eight is not in the room either, and he is eight, and he was told on the Thursday before, and she did it herself.**
- **A water gate is not owned. Giving the days back means the gate never went anywhere, and the gate is still there, and it will still be there in four months, and the only thing that is different is whose turn it is.** Say this in a mouth, in this chapter or in one of the five days after it. **Do not say it in narration and do not say it twice.**
- **The woman of forty-eight in a fourth house at Nine Elms is not in this room, is not asked, is not approached, and nobody stands outside the fourth house.** The Reach's own rule has a hole in it shaped exactly like her and Chapter 0167 found the hole and did not fill it. **This batch may not go near the house and may not fill the hole.**
- **Adrian's twenty-five-day delay expires on this day.** He entered on day 164 that he would do nothing for twenty-five days and that the twenty-fourth is the fifteenth of those twenty-five, and there are ten of them left after it, and **he does not break his own entry to be in a room, and he tells her so at a door in Chapter 0170 and he does not change his mind.**

### Chapter 0185 — day 189, Monday, the thirty-fourth day of the Long Month

**The quarter runs out. Thirty-five days after the hearing on day 154. There is no road in this world that reaches that office, nothing can be sent, and nothing could be prepared.**

**Rules for the chapter:**

- **What comes back is a number, and the reading of that number is not Adrian's.** A case with a question in its eighth column has been on a desk for a hundred and forty-odd days and the return is a figure and a form and a name that is not anybody's.
- **Nothing is answered. Nobody in four hundred miles can act on it and nobody in nine hundred miles can be asked anything about it before the next quarter, and the next quarter is not a date anybody in this city holds.**
- **Do not make the return good news and do not make it bad news.** The finding is that **a thing that was going to arrive on a day and did not is a different kind of information from a thing that arrives**, and that is the whole of what day 189 gives anybody.
- **The eleven days after the midpoint are not summarised in this chapter.** A summary of a cost is the coda of a chapter that has run out of room, and this chapter has a room.
- **The keeper is not rescued in this chapter either, and the second half of her anger is not this chapter's work.** She said a year, in Chapter 0170, in advance, and a year is a year.

## The five prose instructions, from `outline/volume-04.md` §17, and what the first twenty chapters did with them

**Read §17 in the outline. This is what came of it in Batch 0001, so that the second half of the volume does not drift back into the first.**

1. **A chapter may not open by summarising itself, and least of all its ending. The opening sentence states a pressure or an arrival. It does not state the finding, and the finding is the thing the chapter is for.** **Nine openings in Batch 0001 were rewritten for this, five of them because they opened on a craft note about the chapter — *the day is about the bowl and not about the man* — which is the one slot this rule reserves for a thing happening. Do not write a sentence about what the chapter is about.**
2. **The bolded ledger paragraph may not open a chapter, and a figure that is not load-bearing may not appear in bold at all.** **The licence age, the palm line and the fee are not load-bearing in this volume and are not in the first twenty chapters. A figure that is load-bearing is paid for once, in a mouth, attached to a decision, and again only when it changes.** The cost column is recited five times across Batch 0001 and it never changes; **this batch may recite it once and no more.**
3. **The closing coda is cut by at least half and may not enumerate the standing threads.** One thread, one image, one thing that changed and one thing that did not. **A chapter that ends on the sound of a book being recited has not ended, and a chapter that ends on a numbered list has not ended.** **A chapter may end on a figure, a hand, a door, a queue, a rope, a bell, or a sentence somebody said and will not say again, and on nothing else.** The formula *And the last thing on the Nth day of the Long Month is…* stood in eleven chapters of Batch 0001 and now stands in one. **Do not use it.**
4. **The *about N seconds* refrain is used deliberately and sparingly, at most once in a chapter and never twice, and the same limit is set on the two motifs that travel with it — *a person who does not want to be asked*, and *in about nine seconds*.** **Batch 0001 ran seven instances across twenty chapters against 245 across Volume 03's fifty, and the bare sentence *Nobody said anything for about nineteen seconds* is the one to cut first.** **A pause that matters is a thing a person does with their hands.**
5. **The people who carry this volume have a second handle beside the age and the trade and never instead of it** — a name, a habit, a piece of clothing, a thing they do with a pen. **The full list is in `bible/characters.md` §15c and the handles are: Adrian Vale, a name given to him; Hessa Ruun, who counts water on the fingers of her left hand; the keeper of the Redroot gate, a board in her left hand; Nerra Fenn, her hands before her mouth; the woman of about thirty-four who keeps a stall by the wharf, a slate she has never written on and has never explained; Jonah Pike, a printed sheet handed over before a word is said; a man of about thirty-four who keeps a stall, a slate he writes on when he is told not to; Bel Dain, a room with a bench facing the door. The device produced two phantoms in twenty chapters and both were repairs: a woman of about twenty-nine who does not exist and a man of about thirty-nine who was invented to hold a line the chapter said was spoken by somebody who was not in the room. A third is not to be tolerated.**

**And the thing the five exist for: nobody in Volume 03 got stronger. Volume 04's gains so far are a share, a name he did not choose, a month, a date, a gate that came back and a woman who went on a page on purpose. None of them is a power. One of them is the price of a power. All of them are heavier than a power.**

## The prohibitions, and they are the volume's, not this batch's

**From `outline/volume-04.md` §16, and unchanged:**

- **The word *knock* does not appear once in this batch and the correct number of times in Volume 04 is also zero.**
- **The box stays shut.** The strap is untied, the writing round the edge of the wax is unread, the notary has said no six times and may not be improved on, and no chapter opens it and no chapter explains the wax.
- **The room at the far end of the Narrow Mark** is unlooked at in five batches. A chapter may go and look at it, may describe somebody standing in it, or may not; **if it does, the description may not become a description, the knocks may not be used, nobody may open anything, and whoever goes must come back.** This batch's plan does not use it and does not forbid it.
- **The boards under the chapel are not lifted. The chapel stone says nothing and is not repaired. The main breach is closed, dressed, measured and silent.** The five lock sites stay apart and nothing happens at four of them.
- **The woman of forty-eight in a fourth house at Nine Elms is not asked, not approached, and nobody stands outside the fourth house.**
- **Owen Park is not mentioned once.** Nobody may write *he died because*.
- **Marrow stays publicly useful and unaccused.** No scene convicts him and none makes him useless, neither name may be guessed aloud by anybody who has not been given it, and he has still not mentioned the letter to Hattie Park.
- **Wenna Cray's fifth statement of error stands unanswerable and unanswered, and this batch does not answer it.**
- **The four readers are four** and no fifth may be named. **The measurement column is not continuous, the twenty-fifth reading has not been taken since the first of March, and no chapter of this volume takes it.**
- **The two words in about nine rooms are not a name and nobody puts the rooms together. The twenty-eight words on a slate stay face down. The page on the back of a stone stays wrong on purpose.** The eight names at the foot of a hundred-and-forty-year-old page are not read, copied, translated or put into the local language in a room.
- **A delegation is a number with legs.** It has not left, nobody has been asked whether they will go, and the *to open nothing* clause belongs to the woman of twenty-nine and is kept as hers.
- **The compact of eleven lines is not ended. The provisional recognition is not ended. No chapter finds the form that would let a district be described as not recognised. The seat of holder of the pull stays vacant** and is not filled without a room, in daylight, with a date on it.
- **The trestle count is 114 on day 154 and 158 on day 198 and it is not this batch's and is not this volume's to soften, and it is not called by the name of the woman its owner's letter is addressed to.**
- **The four Elms' fourth channel stays shut for the whole volume and a woman of forty-eight in a fourth house is not asked.**
- **Nine miles is the upper road and eleven miles is the Reach.** Do not merge them and do not invent a third distance. Where a sentence needs the settlement seen from Redroot it says *up the road past this city* and not a number.
- **Adrian does not change stage.** Stage 2, Passage holder, in the doing, barred from every roster at his own request. **No chapter in this volume may offer him a workway and he may not ask for one.**

## The checks, and the two that are cheap

1. **Recompute every weekday from day 1 and grep the twenty files for weekday words.** Every weekday word inside a chapter that refers to its own day or to a dated day before it is in scope. **A check list that says *clean* is a claim about twenty files and it is the most expensive sentence in a state layer, because the phase after this one reads it and does not re-run it. Re-run it.**
2. **Subtract.** For every figure in a chapter that has an anchor, do the subtraction from the anchor and not from a neighbouring chapter: the Long Month day number, the days the quarter has left, the days the men have gone unpaid, the days the channel has been shut, the days the junction has gone without water, the days since the day the thing happened. **Nine of Volume 03's nineteen findings were one fault — a figure copied out of a neighbouring chapter instead of computed, in a sentence that reads perfectly.**
3. **Check the date forms by grep.** `of this month`, `of the month`, `of the month after this one`, `of the new month`, `of the Long Month`, `of this flood`, and any month form this batch has not established. **No chapter in this batch may use the first three forms for its own day.**
4. **Check the *knock* count and the Owen Park count by grep. Both must be zero.**
5. **Check the *about N seconds* count, the coda lengths and the ledger-paragraph count by hand, against the targets in the five prose instructions.** **No chapter may carry more than one of the seconds motif, the *person who does not want to be asked* motif, or the *in about nine seconds* motif.**
6. **Check that no chapter states a finding in its first sentence and that no chapter opens on a note about what the chapter is about**, by reading the first two lines of each of the twenty.
7. **Check that every name and every place this batch introduces is established in a room, in daylight, with a date on it, and that none of them is established by narration.**
8. **Check the two distances by grep.** Nine is the upper road; eleven is the Reach; anything that needs a distance it does not have gets *up the road past this city*.
9. **Check that no chapter in this batch rescues the keeper of the Redroot gate, and that no chapter has her say she would say yes again, and that the phrase *the whole of her* is not used about her twice.**

## Length

`PHASE_SYSTEM.md` is the standard: **approximately 2,200–3,200 words for an ordinary chapter, longer where a complete scene, a naming or an emotional payoff needs the room.** Counted with `wc -w` on the files as they stand, **Volume 04 Batch 0001 is a minimum of 2,193, a median of 2,349 and a maximum of 2,940, and that is the figure to beat.** **The three chapters in this batch that may run long are 0175 (a household is asked and says yes), 0185 (the quarter runs out) and 0190 (the batch's cliff).** **Never pad, never split a complete scene to hit a number, never resolve a mystery to get to an ending, and never make a chapter shorter by cutting the thing it was for. Re-count after any repair, not at the end.**

## The rule this run must not break

**A plan is a plan and the pages are not.** The box is shut. The four Elms' fourth channel is shut and a woman of forty-eight in a fourth house is not asked. The sixth reading is not taken and the twenty-fifth reading is not taken. The delegation has not left and nobody has been asked whether they will go, and the only instruction it has is *to open nothing*, and that clause belongs to the woman of twenty-nine. The eight names at the foot of a hundred-and-forty-year-old page are not read. The room at the far end of the Narrow Mark is unlooked at. **And a chapter that resolves a thing this volume is going to spend four movements on is a chapter that has spent the volume's own material on nothing.**

**And the one sentence that is the volume, and it was said once, in Chapter 0154, at a junction, in the local language, and nobody may improve on it and nobody may say it in narration: a gate is not owned, what a household has is the days on it, and the only way a household loses a gate is by agreeing — and if it gives the days it still has the gate.**
